thread:
maya: FYI canary for PR 6028 (longseq workload) is showing sustained mem growth on the worker pods — p95 RSS ~2.8x baseline after ~45m. attaching heap + flamegraph: https://s3.redwood/ci/artifacts/6028/canary-heap.tgz :rotating_light:
chris: ugh. saw the same on staging earlier, looks like kv-cache retention is growing instead of trimming on long prefixes. any quick flags we can toggle? :eyes:
eli: ran a focused microbench against the canary image, results attached: https://perf.redwood/reports/6028-longseq. summary: token throughput stable, 95/99 latency +6%/+12%, mem delta +180MB per replica. flamegraph link: https://s3.redwood/ci/6028/flame.svg
maya: included the heap snapshot (heapdiff) in the s3 bundle. quick check command I used to repro locally:
```bash
./run_bench --model gpt-longseq --seq 8192 --concurrency 8 --duration 1800
```
perfbot: Automated benchmark results for PR 6028 vs baseline:
- p50: +2%
- p95: +6%
- p99: +12%
- mem (RSS): +180MB per replica after 30m
- error rate: no change
(sanity checks passed)
sarah: TL;DR: if p95 > 10% or mem > 100MB we should consider rollback. since p95 is 6% but p99 is 12% and mem +180MB, I lean revert unless we can prove mitigation in next 2h.
chris: quick experiment suggestion: lower kv-eviction.max_shard_size from 1GB -> 256MB and re-run canary. config snippet:
```yaml
kv_cache:
  max_shard_size: 268435456  # 256MB
  eviction_policy: lru
```
maya: applied the reduced shard size on a new canary. after 20m mem dropped ~60MB but still ~+120MB vs baseline. tail latency still spiky at p99.
eli: I think there's a secondary retention path: the attention cache isn't getting released promptly when batch sizes vary. I'm preparing a small diagnostic build to insert explicit kv-cache stats logging and a forced cache trim between requests. pushing draft PR now (WIP).
maya: tagged reviewers @chris @sarah and added the logs to the canary. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6072 (draft)
sarah: OK if hotfix PR isn't green in 2h we revert. can we get a binary revert window estimate?
chris: revert is low-risk; history shows instant rollback is safe for this kind of change. I'll schedule a rolling revert in 30m if no sign of fix.
perfbot: canary monitor update: error rate stable, tail latency spike still present at p99 (~+11%).
maya: initiating revert of PR 6028 now (rolling revert across canary pool). will report once all pods back to baseline image.
chris: ack. after revert we should run the extended bench (1h) to confirm memory slope is back to baseline.
eli: continuing with diagnostic build and will post new flamegraphs. thanks for quick triage everyone :thumbsup:
maya: revert completed, pods back to baseline image, preliminary mem slope looks similar to pre-PR. monitoring for 15m more then will mark canary closed.
sarah: great, follow-up action: eli to open a tracked issue with repro steps, logs, and proposed fix. tag perf for regression tests.
eli: will do, creating issue and linking draft PR.
maya: closing canary thread once post-checks done. thanks all.
